title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This belongs to Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' study, the page-by-page analysis of the stratum M_{0,3} of the Teichmüller tower.
- Pi = Pi_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,inf}, generated by loops l_0, l_1, l_inf with l_0 l_1 l_inf = 1.
- It is enlarged by the symmetry elements rho (the order-3 cyclic permutation of 0,1,inf), sigma_inf / tau_inf (involutions fixing inf) and J' (an anti-holomorphic or reversing symmetry). Inside this enlarged group, rho(x) means conjugation by rho, and so on.
- phi-hat is the extension to this enlarged group of an inertia-preserving automorphism phi of Pi. Its 'multiplier' mu (the lambda of GT) is the exponent on inertia.
- xi, eta (and zeta) are the parameters entering the two fundamental relations (14) and (15). These are essentially the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) and 2-cycle relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller type for a pair (mu, f).

Previous page. Grothendieck derived (52)–(53): the three 'delicate parameters' beta, alpha and beta^{-1} alpha are read off from the values of phi-hat on xi, rho^{-1}(xi) and rho(xi). He remarks that this would let one avoid 'delicate, not yet proved results' of the type zeta = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and eta = beta sigma_inf(beta)^{-1}. Those statements say the relation-parameters are coboundaries for the Z/3 action (via rho) and the Z/2 action (via sigma_inf); they are what justify introducing alpha and beta at all.

This page, step by step.
1. Recapitulation (54):
   - phi-hat(xi) = beta sigma_inf^i;
   - phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi)) = rho J' sigma_inf^{alpha_3} alpha~^{-1}, with alpha~ = alpha tau_inf^{alpha_3};
   - phi-hat(rho(xi)) = sigma_inf^i (beta^{-1} alpha~) sigma_inf^{alpha_3} rho J'. The argument is written rho^{-1}(xi) and corrected by an underbrace to rho(xi); the right side is rewritten as sigma^i (beta^{-1} alpha~) sigma^{alpha_3+i} rho^{-1} J'.
2. Simplifying case (55): alpha_3 = 0, i.e. alpha = alpha~, i.e. alpha lies in Pi_{0,3} itself and not merely in the extension.
3. Inverting the second formula gives phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})) = alpha rho^{-1} J'.
4. Apply the map x -> x rho(x)^{-1} to both sides. The symmetry part rho^{-1} J' cancels and leaves alpha rho(alpha)^{-1}. This gives (56): zeta = phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})) · rho(phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})))^{-1}.
5. So the coboundary form of the 3-cycle parameter is produced explicitly, with the explicit cochain phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})). This already implies the first fundamental formula (14).

What comes next. On the next page this yields: when mu ≡ 1 (mod 3), i.e. nu ≡ 0 (mod 3), the pair of relations (14)+(15) is equivalent to a single relation, (57) or (58). The case mu ≡ -1 is illustrated by the explicit element tau_inf.

Purpose. Grothendieck wants a self-contained description of the solutions u_xi in M_{0,3}^{!≈}(0). It should rest only on the values of phi-hat, not on an unproved nonabelian-H^1 (coboundary) statement, and so reduce the system of fundamental equations.
errors: The third line of (54) is written with argument rho^{-1}(xi) and corrected only by an underbrace to rho(xi). The exponent bookkeeping (sigma_inf^{alpha_3} vs sigma_inf^{alpha_3+i}, and J' vs rho^{-1} J') is not fully consistent between the two writings.
The step from step 3 (inversion) to (56) silently uses commutation rules between J', rho and sigma_inf (e.g. J' rho^{-1} J'^{-1} = rho) that are not restated here.
The argument covers only the special case alpha_3 = 0, so it gives no unconditional proof of zeta = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1}.
Strictly, (56) shows that zeta is a coboundary for the explicit element phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})), which lies in Pi only under alpha_3 = 0.

ideas.what: Expressing the GT-type parameters (the 3-cycle and 2-cycle relation data) as coboundaries x rho(x)^{-1} and x sigma(x)^{-1} for the Z/3 and Z/2 symmetry actions on the profinite free group. Grothendieck flags this as 'delicate, not yet proved'.
ideas.modern_name: Writing f in GT-hat as a coboundary (f = g(y,x)^{-1} g(x,y)-type statements); nonabelian H^1 of finite symmetry groups acting on F-hat_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) in the pro-unipotent setting; discussed for GT-hat by Lochak–Schneps and Ihara in the 1990s

ideas.what: Avoiding that unproved coboundary statement by reading the coboundary data directly from the values of the extended automorphism phi-hat on xi, rho^{-1}(xi), rho(xi), in the extended group generated by Pi_{0,3} and rho, sigma_inf, J'.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of the extended (S_3 × complex-conjugation) fundamental group of M_{0,3}; GT acting on the 'symmetric' orbifold group

ideas.what: Under mu ≡ 1 (mod 3) (nu ≡ 0 mod 3), the 2-cycle and 3-cycle fundamental relations (14),(15) reduce to a single relation (completed on the next page).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997) and Furusho (2011) for other redundancies (pentagon implies hexagons); this specific mod-3 reduction is not known to me in the literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies the coboundary statements zeta = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and eta = beta sigma_inf(beta)^{-1} as open ('délicats non encore démontrés'). He proposes bypassing them via phi-hat values, but carries this out only when alpha_3 = 0.
missed.quote: de faire appel à des résultats délicats non encore démontrés, du type ζ=αρ(α)^{-1}, η=βσ_∞(β)^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether the 2- and 3-cycle relations in GT-hat force coboundary form is a natural nonabelian-cohomology question for profinite free groups. A clean literature reference for the profinite case is not standard.

missed.claim: An explicit formula expressing the 3-cycle parameter as a rho-coboundary via the extended automorphism: zeta = phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})) · rho(phi-hat(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})))^{-1}. Combined with the next page, it reduces the two fundamental relations to one when the multiplier mu ≡ 1 (mod 3).
missed.quote: ζ=φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}))ρ(φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1})))^{-1} qui implique déjà la première formule (14)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a congruence-dependent (mod 3) redundancy among GT-type relations. It is phrased via the S_3-extended group rather than via f alone, which is not a standard viewpoint in the GT literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful technical step in an unpublished, systematic re-derivation of GT-type relations for M_{0,3}. The mod-3-dependent reduction of the 2- and 3-cycle relations to one equation, and the explicit coboundary formula, are not standard in the literature. However, the page is a special case (alpha_3 = 0) of routine-looking manipulations.
transcription_corrections: Throughout (54) the argument is ξ (xi), not β: φ̂(ξ)=βσ_∞^i, φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ))=ρJ'σ_∞^{α_3}α̃^{-1}, etc.
Third line of (54): the left argument is written ρ^{-1}(ξ), with underbrace 'ρ(ξ)'. The right side reads σ_∞^i(β^{-1}α̃)σ_∞^{α_3}ρJ', with underbrace σ_∞^i(β^{-1}α̃)σ_∞^{α_3+i}ρ^{-1}J'.
In (56) the arguments are ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}), not ρ^{-1}(β^{-1}).
First line: 'menant les calculs en termes de φ̂' (likely φ̂ rather than β').
